title: shadeSmooth
body:
## shadeSmooth

Copies the input mesh and sets every face to smooth (enabled true) or flat (enabled false) shading. Smooth shading interpolates normals across faces so tessellated curved surfaces render without facets; positions and topology are unchanged. Use subdivision or smooth when the geometry itself must change.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Smooth shading on hard-edged parts creates dark gradients; follow with weightedNormal or bevel the edges.
- STL publications do not carry shading flags.

Native binding: `shadeSmooth`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | one node | yes | `data` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | true marks every face smooth, so normals are interpolated and curved tessellations render without facets; false marks every face flat, showing each polygon. Vertex positions do not change. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` |
